name: How do I design a kitchen for an older Los Angeles home with uneven walls or floors?

mainEntity.name: How do I design a kitchen for an older Los Angeles home with uneven walls or floors?
mainEntity.text: How do I design a kitchen for an older Los Angeles home with uneven walls or floors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older Los Angeles homes frequently have walls that are out of square, floors that slope, and framing that does not match modern cabinet dimensions. That makes custom kitchen design especially useful because it can be built around the reality of the structure instead of forcing standard sizes into an imperfect shell. The process should start with accurate field measurements, not just architectural drawings, because small discrepancies can affect cabinet fit, appliance alignment, and countertop installation. In many cases, scribing panels, filler adjustments, and custom end panels are necessary to achieve a polished result. If the floor is uneven, it may be worth correcting it before cabinets are installed, since a level base improves countertop and appliance performance. Homeowners should also plan for how gaps, trim, and reveal lines will be handled so the finished kitchen looks intentional rather than patched together. This is one area where experienced design-build coordination matters a great deal.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older homes often need custom kitchen solutions because walls and floors are rarely perfectly square or level. Careful measurement, tailored cabinetry, and finish carpentry help hide imperfections and create a cleaner built-in appearance.
